newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities ended lower.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities ended lower.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended lower across the board in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Wednesday.

"Both treasury bill yields and bond prices eased slightly today but it did not have an impact on the market. The interbank rate, on the other hand, rose slightly. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.15/2.10 percent compared with Tuesday's yield of 2.35/2.30 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.70/1.65 percent against 1.95/1.90 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$101.50/101.60 from Tuesday's close of S$101.95/102.05, September 2001 at S$98.47/98.52 versus S$98.83/98.88 and June 2003 at S$97.97/98.02 against S$98.30/98.35.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent from Tuesday's 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent.
